name: Type I fibre (slow-twitch)
short_description: A slow-twitch, oxidative skeletal muscle fibre built for endurance: a single unbranched, cylindrical cell running centimetres long (~40-60 um across), with hundreds of nuclei flattened at the PERIPHERY just under the sarcolemma, regular cross-striations (A/I bands, Z-disc to Z-disc sarcomeres) alongside lengthwise myofibrils, and dense packing of mitochondria and myoglobin that give it a deep red colour and an essentially inexhaustible aerobic ATP supply, fed by a rich surrounding capillary bed.

FAIL on framing: both ends are closed, rounded caps fully inside the canvas, including a full circular end-on cross-section disc of nuclei at each tip -- exactly the 'short stubby cell that fits entirely inside the frame' failure the brief calls out, reading as a capsule floating in empty space rather than a fibre running the length of a muscle. Fix-prompt: force both ends to run off the canvas edge, drop the end-on cross-section discs.

textbook.3: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; escalated after 2 flash fails on framing. Used as final. Fibre now runs out of the top-right and bottom-left corners of the frame, no end caps. Cutaway window shows both patterns at once: transverse A/I banding with visible grey Z-lines across the fibre's width AND fine lengthwise myofibril hatching underneath, exactly the 'both real, check the axis' case the brief warns about. Dense mitochondria packed in a continuous subsarcolemmal rim (orange with cristae detail), deep brick-red sarcolemma, capillaries branching organically alongside. Verified by anchor-sampling every leader line against the raw base image (not the rasterised SVG, whose dot marker sits on top of the anchor pixel): mitochondrion/myofibril/i_band/z_disc/sarcomere/a_band/capillary/nucleus all land on the correct structure; satellite_cell lands precisely on a separate small pale wedge-shaped cell tucked at the fibre's outer edge, distinct in colour and shape from the blue-grey myonuclei (see the nucleus-vs-satellite-cell note below). No baked text found on inspection of magnified quadrants. No border on any of the 4 edges.

reference: pass (2026-08-21). Wikimedia Commons / Berkshire Community College Bioscience Image Library 'Muscle Tissue Skeletal Muscle Fibers (40153601630).jpg', CC0 1.0, H&E-stained teased longitudinal skeletal muscle fibres. Viewed at full resolution: several fibres show fine continuous cross-striation and multiple dark elongated nuclei pressed against the periphery, never centred -- counted at least 10 distinct peripheral nuclei across the frame. No baked-in text, scale bar, border or watermark; used as downloaded, no cleaning needed. Honest caveats (recorded in render.md section 2): this is a teased histological section with several fibres visible, not a single free-standing isolated cell, though teasing keeps each fibre close to individually resolvable; and plain H&E does not distinguish fibre type at all, so nothing in this plate identifies these specific fibres as Type I rather than Type II -- the type-specific colour and mitochondrial density in the renders are sourced from the literature (render.md section 1), not from this micrograph. Two ATPase-stained fibre-type candidates found on Commons were both pathological specimens and were not used.
nucleus_vs_satellite_cell: Open question from the brief, resolved: in the textbook (and 3d, watercolor) renders, the fibre is shown two ways at once -- blue-grey elongated ellipses (the myonuclei) and separate small pale/white teardrop- or wedge-shaped cells with their own smaller grey-purple nucleus (the satellite cells). The teal/dark outline that first looked like 'the sarcolemma' is actually only the edge of the CUTAWAY WINDOW cut into the fibre to reveal the myofibril interior, not the fibre's true outer surface -- that outer surface is the edge of the whole red cylinder against the background. The blue-grey myonuclei sit in the ring of sarcoplasm between the cutaway-window edge and that true outer surface, i.e. peripherally WITHIN the fibre, just inside its real sarcolemma -- the correct location for a myonucleus. The pale teardrop cells sit further out still, perched at the fibre's true outer edge with a distinctly different colour, shape and (smaller) nucleus of their own -- consistent with a satellite cell wedged between the sarcolemma and the basal lamina, a genuinely different structure, not a mislabelled myonucleus. Checked by anchor-sampling both the 'nucleus' and 'satellite_cell' labels in all three illustrated styles against the raw base images: in every case 'nucleus' lands on a blue-grey ellipse embedded in the fibre body, and 'satellite_cell' lands on a separate pale wedge cell at the true edge, so the two labels are already correctly and honestly distinguished in this set's labels.json files -- no relabelling was needed, only the reasoning was worth writing down since the picture is genuinely ambiguous at a glance.
decision: used as final; single coherent fibre running out of frame at both ends, correct A/I banding plus lengthwise myofibril texture, dense subsarcolemmal mitochondria, deep red, capillaries, satellite cell correctly distinguished from myonuclei.
